answer: Local merchant receipt proof stops duplicate aliases. A new alias must collect receipts from five local merchants in one town over 30 days, such as a delta timber yard and an ivory workshop, each receipt naming the alias and date. One operator cannot place dozens of aliases there without merchants noticing repeat faces and orders. Receipts go to a ledger, so identical receipt numbers or matching purchase lists across aliases trigger an audit. Auditors recheck 10 percent of new aliases each month; a proven fake loses its license, pays 50 POA per fake alias, and sits out 12 epochs.
